course: NISM Series XXI-B: Portfolio Managers Certification Examination
unit_name: Performance Measurement and Evaluation of Portfolio Managers
overview: This unit is the Report Card of the portfolio management process. It explains how to calculate returns accurately and, more importantly, how to judge if those returns were due to a manager's skill or just luck. For the NISM exam, you must master return calculation methods like TWRR and understand risk-adjusted ratios like Sharpe and Treynor. This chapter is critical because SEBI has strict rules on how performance is reported to clients.

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: The standard way to measure a manager's performance by removing the effect of client cash flows.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: TWRR breaks the investment period into sub-periods every time money is added or removed. It calculates return for each sub-period separately and then compounds them. This measures the Manager's Skill, not the Investor's Timing.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: SEBI mandates TWRR for PMS performance reporting because it fairly compares managers.
complete_concept_explanation.formula_explanation: Multiply 1 plus each sub-period return and subtract 1 from the final value.
exam_traps: Confusing TWRR with MWRR. MWRR is affected by cash flow timing.
Using TWRR for tax calculations. IRR/XIRR (MWRR) is used for that.

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: Extra return earned per unit of total risk taken.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: Sharpe Ratio compares excess return to total volatility. Higher Sharpe means better risk-adjusted performance.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: It helps judge whether returns are due to skill or excessive risk-taking.
complete_concept_explanation.formula_explanation: (Portfolio Return − Risk-Free Rate) divided by Standard Deviation.
exam_traps: Sharpe uses Standard Deviation, not Beta.

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: Extra return earned per unit of market risk taken.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: Treynor Ratio measures return relative to systematic risk using Beta. It assumes the portfolio is well-diversified.
complete_concept_explanation.formula_explanation: (Portfolio Return − Risk-Free Rate) divided by Beta.
exam_traps: Treynor uses Beta, Sharpe uses Standard Deviation.

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: Extra return earned above expected return based on risk taken.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation: Alpha compares actual return with CAPM expected return. Positive Alpha means outperformance.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: Active PMS fees are justified only if consistent positive Alpha is generated.
complete_concept_explanation.formula_explanation: Actual Return minus CAPM expected return.
exam_traps: High return does not always mean positive Alpha.

important_differences.clear_explanation: Sharpe uses Total Risk (Standard Deviation). Treynor uses Systematic Risk (Beta).
TWRR evaluates Manager performance. MWRR evaluates Investor experience.

frequently_asked_exam_areas: Mandatory use of TWRR for PMS reporting.
Calculation of Sharpe and Treynor ratios.
quick_revision_summary: Performance measurement distinguishes Skill vs Luck.
Performance reporting must be transparent and periodic.
